column3: NKJV includes “to you,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “they will do these things.”
NKJV lacks “their” before “time,” as does the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “when their hour comes.”
NKJV has “My Father,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the Father.”
NKJV has “into all truth” and “whatever He hears,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “in all the truth” and “whatever He will hear.”
NKJV has “He will take,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the present “He takes.”
NKJV includes “because I go to the Father,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it and reads “you no longer see Me.”
NKJV has “I will tell you,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “I will announce to you.” “Allegories” is rendered “figurative language.”
